Chapter 11: Teaching the Next Generation—Passing Down the Wisdom of Wintering.
You know, kids are always watching us. They don’t just listen to what we say—they soak up how we actually live, every little detail. In a world that’s always pushing us to do more and move faster, it’s all too easy to send the message that taking a break means you’re falling behind, or that rest is somehow a weakness.
But what if we could show them a different way?
Imagine this: there’s a parent who notices their child feeling anxious about school. Instead of pushing harder, they decide to try something new—a “quiet hour” every evening. No screens, no homework, just time to read, draw, or simply be themselves. At first, the child squirms, asking for distractions—honestly, who wouldn’t? But gradually, that quiet hour becomes something special. It turns into a little oasis, a chance to unwind, to talk, to reconnect as a family.
Here’s something to pay attention to—most adults underestimate just how much their own habits shape the young people around them. When kids see us taking breaks, reaching out for help, or practicing a bit of self-care, they learn it’s okay to do the same. The lessons of wintering aren’t only for those tough moments or crises. These are skills everyone can use.
There’s also the story of a teacher who, after struggling with burnout, decided to open up to their students about the importance of rest. They encouraged kids to notice when they felt overwhelmed. To take small breaks. To support each other in the classroom. And slowly, the whole atmosphere changed—it became kinder, more accepting, a place where making mistakes wasn’t the end of the world, but just part of learning.
Passing down the wisdom of wintering—it’s really an act of care, isn’t it? It means breaking the old cycle of exhaustion and building a culture where well-being actually matters. When adults show self-compassion and balance, we’re giving the next generation permission to do the same.
So, here’s the key takeaway: by living these lessons ourselves, we help kids grow up with a healthier, more loving relationship to rest and renewal. And honestly, isn’t that what we all want for them?
